Order No.09 / Dated : 09.08.2023
1.

Instant writ petition has been filed for seeking a direction upon the respondent for not disturbing the possession of the petitioner over the land pertaining the Plot Nos.606 & 607, Jamabandi No.22,
Mouza Saharkol No.21, District Pakur and further to restore the proceeding of L.A. Case No.03 of 2007- 2008.
2.

The petitioner is mainly aggrieved by order dated 24.09.2020 passed by respondent no.4, District Land Acquisition Officer, Pakur whereby and whereunder the objection filed by petitioner has been held to be time barred under Section 5(a) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

3. As per the case of the petitioner, the District Land Acquisition Officer initiated proceeding for acquisition of land in District Municipal Area for the purposed shop and hatia by L.A. Case No.03 of 2007-2008.
The petitioner was not aware of the said proceeding and he was not served notice in the said land acquisition case.

sentences.text: 5. It is submitted by learned counsel on behalf of State that after acquisition of land, the said plot has already been allotted to respondent no.5-Municpal Corporation.
After completing the due process under Sections 4, 6, 11 & 12, possession has been delivered under Section 16.

Notice of the Land Acquisition case was duly served, the copy of which has been enclosed by Annexure G & H.
6.
Process of land acquisition was initiated vide letter no.96 dated 12.02.2007 with respect to 11.56 acres of land of village.

Preliminary and final notifications were published in terms of Sections 4 and 6 of the Act in the official Gazette on 31.05.2007 and in daily newspaper on 26.05.2007 and 20.06.2007, and objections were received from the objectors.
From annexure G and H of the counter affidavit filed on behalf of the State, it appears that substance of the public notice was given in the locality under Sections 9 and 12 of the Act.
Compensation has been assessed and final order passed on 05.05.2008 and award made.
7. Compensation has not been received by the petitioner under the award although amount has been deposited in treasury.
8. Question for determination is whether the Award under the old 1894 Act will lapse under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act?
This Court is of the view that the Award under the old Act will not lapse for the reason that the amount has been not been received.

From the impugned order, it is abundantly clear that the compensation amount had already been deposited in the treasury and notices have been served to the petitioner to receive the compensation amount, but they did not turn up to receive the amount.
It has
been held in Indore Development Authority (LAPSE-5 J.) v. Manoharlal, (2020) 8 SCC 129 366.5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case a person has been tendered the compensation as provided under Section 31(1) of the 1894 Act, it is not open to him to claim that acquisition has lapsed under Section 24(2) due to non-payment or non-deposit of compensation in court.
The obligation to pay is complete by tendering the amount under Section 31(1).
The landowners who had refused to accept compensation or who sought reference for higher compensation, cannot claim that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

Plea of the petitioner that the proceeding under the 1894 Act has lapsed is therefore not tenable in view of the ratio referred to above, since the award had been made, compensation amount deposited in the treasury and tendered to the petitioner.
Further, where the award has been made it takes the forms of a decree, which cannot be challenged before a writ Court.
